entry.title: How to Choose Your MVP Tech Stack
entry.summary: Choosing a tech stack for an MVP is not a technical decision. It is a product decision with technical constraints. Getting it wrong costs more time than getting it right costs thought. Most engineers default to what they know best. That is a reasonable starting point and often the wrong answer for the product stage you are actually in. Stage determines stack: a validation-stage MVP needs a different stack than a scale-stage product, and treating them the same way is expensive. Low-code is a legitimate production option in 2026: Bubble, FlutterFlow, and Glide support real production workloads; dismissing them on principle without evaluating them is bias, not engineering. entry.title: I built an npm malware scanner in Rust because npm audit isn't enough
entry.summary: Last week I ran npm install on a new project. 847 packages downloaded in twelve seconds. And I thought: what if one of those just stole my AWS keys? Not a crazy thought. It happened before. In 2018, event-stream got a new maintainer who slipped in code that stole cryptocurrency wallets. Two million weekly downloads.
